notes:
I can't give you the Proverbs 19 notes yet. My research tools stopped working before I read any of the commentary pages, so I have no sources to report from.

Here's what happened. I asked for six pages at once:
- Enduring Word on Proverbs 19
- Precept Austin's Proverbs 19 commentary
- Ellicott's, Gill's and the Pulpit Commentary's notes on Proverbs 19 (on biblehub.com)
- The NET Bible notes on Proverbs 19

Whether those pages loaded is unclear. A mistake in my own code meant I couldn't open the results, and before I could fix it I hit the limit on tool calls for this turn. None of that content reached me.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse notes from memory, because I'd have no real URLs to cite for them.

If you reply (even just "continue"), the tools should work again. I'll start with the six pages above to cover the traditional reading of verses 1–29. Then I'll search the tradition-specific sites for verses where views are likely to differ:
- **v. 14:** where a prudent wife comes from, and God's providence
- **v. 17:** kindness to the poor as a loan to the LORD, and the reward. This is also the likeliest place for prosperity-teaching material, and for Catholic teaching on almsgiving.
- **v. 18:** discipline, and "do not be party to his death"
- **v. 21:** human plans and God's purpose, where Reformed and Wesleyan views on God's sovereignty may differ

To avoid running out of calls again, you could also limit the first round to some verses (say 1–15) and do the rest next.
